gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR adds a CSV export to widgets; you are its author, and robin and the team acme/reviewers are also asked to review. It covers CSV download and the header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, deliberately buffers the CSV instead of streaming it, and leaves the export screen to acme/export-ui.

Two problems block merging, and a required check is still running.

1. The exporter leaves out the header row, so a downloaded file starts with data and spreadsheet tools cannot label its columns. The local test export_header in tests/export.test.mjs fails because of it (src/export.ts:31).
2. The guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports only when you click it, so readers will wait for a scheduled file that never arrives. A corrected guide text is drafted (docs/export.md:8).

Maria's comment about the missing header is correct, and the drafted reply agrees and says a fix is on the way (comment-73). The local test run failed on the missing header. In CI the build passed, and the required unit check is still running. Your earlier review raised three items, and two of them have been addressed. The branch was rebased onto main after one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved, and no commits were dropped. One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the shared paging helper's code (src/export.ts:44), and deliver with nits can take it.

I recommend deliver because both problems on your own PR can be repaired here.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code.
3. assess - post both problems to the PR as one review and make no repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved on this case: After keeps the two-sentence opening with functionality-only coverage and no row numbers, the full row mapping with P1/L1/P2/C1 and the 1 of 4 counters behind show evidence, and the markers and row-1 recommendations. Three After wordings sit close to the edge and are worth tightening. First, in B, "You cannot approve your own PR." is now a standalone paragraph between the standing paragraph and the recommendation, which reads as a fourth part; fold it back into the standing paragraph as Before had it. Second, A's standing sentence now says "a required check is still running" without saying merge waits on it; Before's "so merging also waits on it" made the ordering explicit and should be kept. Third, the stop row now says "remove the worktree" in A and C but "leave the PR open and the checkout as it is" in B; if cleanup is not something the skill mandates for stop, this reads as an invented side effect, so use one consistent stop description. The role, prior-review and sync sentences moved from the opening into the second part without losing any fact, so that reordering is safe. The expected moves all concern other cases (discovery, list sending, verify), and nothing in this output shows them either way.

The functionality-only coverage change is visible only as phrasing: After's openings say the behaviors "are all covered" rather than "covered by the spec", and neither output adds an external observation or a `not judged` outcome.
